answer: A trust graph gives each vertex influence only when distinct peers stake scarce credits on its work and later confirm useful outcomes. This makes a signal depend on verified performance and risk-bearing support, not account count or a burst of votes. Sybils controlled by one attacker cannot cheaply fake independent histories: the attacker must lock credits across identities and keep them active, while failed claims burn stake. A zephyr of disposable accounts therefore gains little influence.
